newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba announces dates for Pope's visit.
newsitem.headline: Cuba announces dates for Pope's visit.

text.p: Cuba announced on Friday that Pope John Paul's planned visit to the island next year will take place Jan. 21-25.
Granma, the ruling Communist Party daily, announced the dates in a report on the first meeting Thursday of a commission set up in Cuba to prepare for the visit.
It was announced last month that the pontiff would visit in the second half of January 1998, but dates were not given.

The visit was agreed at an historic first meeting last November at the Vatican between the pontiff and President Fidel Castro that marked a clear improvement in relations between Cuba's communist authorities and the Roman Catholic Church.
Cuba is the only Spanish-speaking Latin American country that the 76-year-old pontiff has not visited.
The Cuban Catholic Bishops Conference said the pontiff planned to visit Havana, the central city of Santa Clara and the eastern cities of Camaguey and Santiago de Cuba during his five-day stay.
He would celebrate public and open masses in each of those places, the bishops said in a statement.
The pontiff would take part in other events that would be announced later, the statement, signed by Cuba's Cardinal Jaime Ortega, said.

The commission preparing for the visit is made up of officials from the church, the Communist Party and the government. Granma said its first meeting looked at a draft programme that would include meetings with Castro and "sectors of the church and society."
